name: Pulmonary Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Pulmonary Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Current or prior history of cigarette smoking
Characteristic cystic and nodular lesions on high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest
Lung biopsy demonstrating granulomatous infiltration with CD1a-positive Langerhans cells
Exclusion of other cystic lung diseases such as lymphangioleiomyomatosis and emphysema

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic HRCT findings plus histopathological confirmation or typical clinical and radiologic features in a smoker
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Biopsy may be avoided if clinical and radiologic features are classic in a smoker

pathognomonic.notes: Often recurrent and may be the initial presentation

laboratory: Mild leukocytosis or normal blood counts
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: HRCT showing upper and mid lung zone cysts and nodules
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; BRAF V600E mutation reported in some cases
other: Bronchoalveolar lavage may show increased CD1a-positive Langerhans cells
Pulmonary function tests often reveal reduced diffusion capacity

distinguishingFeatures: Occurs almost exclusively in women of childbearing age
Diffuse thin-walled cysts without nodules on HRCT
Associated with tuberous sclerosis complex in some cases
Predominantly lower lobe fibrosis and honeycombing
Absence of nodular lesions typical of PLCH

references: Vassallo R, Ryu JH. Pulmonary Langerhans' cell histiocytosis. Clin Chest Med. 2004 Jun;25(2):561-71.
Tazi A. Adult pulmonary Langerhans' cell histiocytosis. Eur Respir J. 2006 Sep;27(6):1272-85.
Yousem SA. Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis: a review. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2000 Oct;124(10):1369-73.
